purpose: A disposable five-minute trial of a pinned, real Omarchy guest running client-side in a browser

referenceProfile.browser: Current stable Chromium with hardware acceleration enabled
referenceProfile.host: Four modern performance CPU cores and 8 GiB available RAM
referenceProfile.network: 100 Mbps down, 20 ms RTT, empty HTTP cache
referenceProfile.measurement: Three cold runs and three warm runs; release thresholds apply to the median unless a percentile is named

gates.assertion: The image records the exact upstream Omarchy repository and a full immutable commit SHA.
The running guest is x86_64 Arch Linux and its installed Omarchy tree matches the release manifest.
The compositor process and version evidence come from real Hyprland inside the guest.
Visible desktop frames are tagged as guest framebuffer frames, and all journey input receives a guest acknowledgement.
A reviewer can correlate menu, terminal, tiling, workspace, and theme changes with guest logs; no HTML reproduction is shown as the desktop.
A cold reference run reaches an interactive desktop within 45 seconds.
A cached reference run reaches an interactive desktop within 15 seconds.
An unsupported browser, failed asset, or guest panic produces an honest recoverable error instead of a fake desktop.
The guest reports a 1600x900 display and the canvas backing store is device-pixel-correct.
Desktop, menu, terminal, tiling, and changed-theme screenshots stay within approved reference tolerances.
Fullscreen and fitted-window modes remain sharp, correctly letterboxed, and free of clipping at DPR 1 and 2.
Keyboard, modifiers, pointer motion, buttons, wheel, focus recovery, and browser shortcut alternatives reach the guest.
95th-percentile input-to-frame latency is at most 150 ms on the reference profile.
Every required five-minute journey step passes with guest acknowledgement.
Reset destroys the disposable overlay and returns to the pristine pinned image.
Frame rate is at least 20 FPS at p50 and 12 FPS at p05 during the journey.
Peak browser memory does not exceed 2560 MiB and no runtime crash occurs.
After desktop-ready, no black-frame interval exceeds two seconds.
The document is cross-origin isolated with COOP and COEP, and reports SharedArrayBuffer availability.
Large guest artifacts support byte ranges and immutable versioned caching; WebAssembly has the correct media type.
The five-minute run has no uncaught page error, console error, or unexpected external guest network request.
Omarchy, QEMU, kernel, firmware, fonts, themes, wallpapers, and packaged applications have recorded licenses and notices.
Corresponding source obligations and Omarchy name/logo permission are cleared before public launch.
